name: Color Systems
summary: A production color palette is a small, role-based system of tokens — not a growing list of hex values picked per component.
description: Color theory tells you which hues harmonise; a color system tells you how many colors you're allowed to ship and what each one is for. The failure mode in most generated and hand-built UIs is the same: designers pick a fresh hex whenever they need 'a slightly different gray' or 'a softer blue,' and the palette quietly grows past the point where hierarchy is legible. Mature systems cap themselves. A typical product UI uses no more than ~10 distinct colors total: one primary, one secondary or accent, a single neutral ramp of 5–7 grays, and 3–4 semantic colors (success, warning, error, info). Everything else — hovers, disabled states, surfaces, borders — is a tonal step derived from those base hues, not a new color. The discipline is enforced through tokens: once `--color-text-muted` exists, no component should ever inline `#6b7280` again. Mix that with one consistent neutral temperature (warm or cool grays, not both) and the palette stays coherent at any scale.
implications: Define colors by role (primary, accent, neutral, semantic, surface) before picking hex values
Cap a product UI at ~10 distinct base colors; brand/marketing sites can stretch to ~12
Generate tonal ramps (5–9 steps) from each base hue instead of inventing new colors for hovers, borders, and backgrounds
Pick one neutral temperature — all warm grays or all cool grays — and never mix them accidentally
Every color in the codebase should be a token reference; raw hex in component styles is a smell
Semantic colors (success/warning/error/info) are reserved for meaning, not decoration — don't use the error red for a heading accent
Audit the rendered page: count distinct hex values in computed styles. If it exceeds 10–12, the palette has drifted
violations: A single page using 15+ distinct hex values across components
Three near-identical grays (#6b7280, #6c7280, #707070) coexisting because each component picked its own
Mixing warm grays (#78716c) and cool grays (#6b7280) in the same interface without intent
Inlining hex values in component styles instead of referencing a token
Using the semantic 'error' red as a decorative accent, breaking its signal value
Adding a new color every time a designer wants a 'slightly different' shade instead of using an existing tonal step
No defined neutral ramp — grays are picked ad hoc per component
sources: Material Design 3 — Color system and tonal palettes (Google).
IBM Carbon Design System — Color tokens and role-based palette structure.
Refactoring UI — Adam Wathan & Steve Schoger (2018), chapter on building a color palette from tonal ramps.
